 SUBTASK 27-31-00-865-047

 (3) Do this task: "Null Procedure - Mach Trim Actuator" (PAGEBLOCK 27-31-00/201).
 SUBTASK 27-31-00-735-048

 (4) Do the friction and balance test of the elevator surface:
 (a) Move the control columns in a longitudinal direction through full travel 20 times.

 CAUTION: DO NOT PUT A LOAD OF MORE THAN 65 POUND ON THE ELEVATORS AT
 ONE TIME. IF THE LOAD IS TOO HEAVY, IT CAN CAUSE DAMAGE TO THE
 ELEVATORS.
 (b) Measure the breakaway forces:
 1) Hold the captain's control column at the neutral position.
 2) Push the elevator with your hand until the trailing edge of each elevator aligns with
 the index mark, then release (Figure 505).
 (c) If the elevator trailing edge moves down from the index mark, do the balance adjustment
 (SRM 51-60-04).
 (d) If one of the two trailing edges do not stay at the index mark, use the spring scale to
 measure the force required to move them back.
 1) Measure the force that you use to move the trailing edge up 0.75 ±0.15 inch from
 the index mark (which is referred to as the up force).
 2) Make a record of this force.
 3) Measure the force that you use to move the trailing edge down 0.75 ±0.15 inch from
 the index mark (which is referred to as the down force).
 4) If the down force is less than the up force, do the balance adjustment (SRM
 51-60-04).
 5) If the down force is greater than the up force, calculate the sum of these two forces.
 a) If the sum of these two forces is less than 16 pound, do the test of the elevator
 limit travel.
 b) If the sum of these two forces is more than 16 pounds, do the elevator balance
 panel test (PAGEBLOCK 27-31-41/501).
 SUBTASK 27-31-00-865-059

 (5) Do this task: "Put the Elevator Hydraulic Systems A and B Back to the Condition Before the
 Pressure Removal" (PAGEBLOCK 27-31-00/201).

 X = D - W Where D = value on the dial indicator W = 0.0000155 multiplied by the
 total of the two weights

 (d) Measure the play of the right hinge joint:
 1) Attach the dial indicator to the right side.

 3) Slowly add the two weights to the left stabilizer end near the front spar.
 4) Write down the value from the dial indicator.
 5) Slowly remove the two weights.
 6) Calculate the play of the right bearing:
 Y = D - W Where D = value on the dial indicator W = 0.0000155 multiplied by the
 total of the two weights
 NOTE: If the quantity is negative, Y = 0.

 satisfactory. The test permits you to monitor the functions of the flap system on the ground with

 alternate for the system test.

 is correct before you do the operational test.

 flight roller.

 (2) Do a test of the No. 1 autoslat computer operation:

titulo: System Test - Leading Edge Autoslat System

referencias.titulo: LEADING EDGE FLAP AND SLAT CONTROL SYSTEM -

procedimento:
(1) Autoslat system components used in this test are the No. 1 and No. 2 Autoslat Computers
 (ASC), the Angle of Airflow (AOA) Sensors, and the antiskid control unit.
 (2) The Stall Warning system is activated when the angle of attack increases to cause a stall
 warning to appear at the stick shakers.
 The AOA trip angle changes with airspeed, flap position and if the airplane is near the ground.
 These different trip angles are calculated by the stall warning computer.
 (3) All angle of airflow vane angles used in this test are referenced to the angle of airflow test
 fixture protractor. The angle of airflow vane angles given must be corrected for each individual
 vane offset.
 The vane offset is stamped on the trailing edge of each angle of airflow vane. When testing the
 left angle of airflow vane, the vane offset must be added to the test angle requirements; when
 testing the right vane, the vane offset must be subtracted from the test angle requirements.
 (4) The sign convention for the AOA vane angles specified in this test is the same for the left and
 the right AOA sensor vanes. On the calibrator tool, the numbers below the zero point of the
 main scale are positive degrees (= positive angle of attack). The numbers above the zero point
 of the main scale are negative degrees.
 (5) The alpha COMPARE HI and COMPARE LO indicator lights on the face of the computers will
 come on and go off at various steps of this procedure. These lights should be disregarded
 except in the "Dynamic Alpha Compare" section of the test, where the test steps describe the
 status of the lights.
SUBTASK 27-83-00-865-023

 WARNING: MAKE SURE THAT PERSONS AND EQUIPMENT ARE CLEAR OF THE TE FLAPS
 AND THE LE FLAPS AND SLATS DURING THE TEST. FAST MOVEMENT OF THE
 FLAPS CAN CAUSE INJURY TO PERSONS OR DAMAGE TO EQUIPMENT.
 (1) Supply system B hydraulic power (PAGEBLOCK 27-81-00/201).

titulo: Inspection of the Electrical Bonding Jumpers in the Fuel System
procedimento:
(1) This task contains visual and mechanical inspections of the electrical bonding jumpers in the
 fuel system.
 (2) Do not flex, bend or kink the bonding jumpers more than is necessary. If the bonding jumpers
 are moved too much, it can cause the loss of tin plating on the wire braid of the bonding
 jumper.
 (3) When you inspect the bonding jumpers you may see black or brown deposits on the wire braid.
 This can occur when there is a deterioration of the tin plating on the bonding jumper and the
 copper in the wire reacts with the sulfur compounds. This discoloration is not a problem unless
 the wire braid contains broken strands. If the bonding jumper has broken strands, then you
 must replace the bonding jumper.
 (4) When you inspect the bonding jumpers, inspect for loose clamps and corrosion.

(1) Use a microbial detection kit or laboratory standard test to check the fuel/water samples taken
 from each fuel tank. A positive result for microbial contamination requires action that may
 include a biocide treatment or physical removal of the growth from the fuel tanks.
 (2) These are the approved microbial test kit, COM-4806:
 (a) FUELSTAT RESINAE

 (e) The fuel samples can also be sent to a laboratory for testing. IP385 is the Institute for
 Petroleum's test for microbial contamination.
 (3) All instructions supplied with the detection kits should be followed closely. It is important to
 retest if a detection test shows microbial contamination. Differences in the fuel/water sample
 and the ability of the detection kits to consistently measure the level of microbial growth make it
 important to retest and verify test results. Do not compare the test results between the different
 types of detection kits.
 (4) All time intervals listed in this task are recommendations. There is no MMEL or scheduled
 maintenance requirements for testing for microbial contamination.

titulo: Biocide Treatment of Fuel Tanks - Metered Injection Cart
procedimento:
(1) There are two methods to add biocide treatment to the fuel tanks:
 (a) portable biocide injection hydrant cart, COM-1781
 (b) Overwing fuel port
 (2) Do this task if a metered injection cart is available.
 (3) If you need to add biocide without a metered injection cart, then do the overwing fill port task.
 (4) There are two types of metered-injection carts:
 (a) Adjustable metered injection cart
 (b) Non-adjustable metered injection cart
 (5) ADJUSTABLE METERED INJECTION CART;
 This type of metered injection cart is equipped with an adjustable concentration setting. You
 can adjust the concentration setting from tank to tank.
 (6) NON-ADJUSTABLE METERED INJECTION CART;
 This type of metered injection cart is not field adjustable. You cannot adjust the concentration
 setting from tank to tank. You can recalibrate the cart (in a maintenance shop) to achieve the
 desired 270 ppm concentration for Biobor JF additive, G00452, or 100 ppm concentration for
 Kathon FP1.5 biocide, G02347. To account for the typical fuel remaining on-board after a flight,
 a procedure is given to recalibrate the cart to 1.5 times the usual setting. This method will allow
 the correct concentration of treated fuel to be added to the fuel tanks.
 (7) Biocide treatment is used to kill microbial growth within the fuel tank. The process requires that
 the biocide be mixed at a specified concentration with fuel and allowed to soak for a period of
 time. After soaking, the biocide treated fuel may be burned through the engines.
 (8) Two biocidal fuel additives are certified by the airframe and engine manufactures. These are:

RAM ALL 28-11-00

 D6-37569 Mar 25/2015

 (a) Biobor JF additive, G00452 - manufactured by Hammonds
 (b) Kathon FP1.5 biocide, G02347 - manufactured by Rohm & Haas Company
 NOTE: Biobor JF additive, G00452, and Kathon FP1.5 biocide, G02347, have not been
 approved in some geographic areas. Local regulatory agencies should be
 consulted with respect to approval status.
 (9) Obey all Health and Safety precautions specified by the manufacturer related to the use of
 biocide.
 (10) It is recommended to do this task with no fuel or a minimum fuel load (after a flight, before fuel
 servicing). It is not necessary to defuel the aircraft before you begin the biocide treatment.

titulo: Alternative Procedures for Fuel Tank Leak Detection
procedimento:
(1) The best leak detection procedure is usually to find the leak externally with talcum powder and
 then to find the internal leak with the air pressure and soap bubble procedure ("backblowing").
 That procedure is given in the above task: Leak Detection and Repair.
 (2) This task contains alternative procedures used to find a leak. These procedures can be used if
 backblowing is not possible, or if it fails to show all of the leaks. This task also contains the
 internal pressure and bubble procedure which can be used to find external leak locations after
 an airplane is defueled. These are the procedures:
 (a) Pressure Box Application
 (b) Dye Injection Procedure
 (c) Internal Pressure and Bubble Procedure

procedimento:
(1) After you find the external leak point and the internal leak source, find the point where the leak
 path goes through the seal plane. The area where you saw the bubble or the dye on the inner
 surface of the tank is usually the point where the leak path goes through the seal plane. But if
 there is a bad hidden seal (an injection seal, prepack seal, or faying surface seal), fuel can go
 into the structure and go a long distance before it shows at the external leak point. If there is a
 bad hidden seal and you repair only the seal where the bubbles or dye were shown, it is
 possible that the repair is only temporary. These leaks can occur again many times until you
 find the correct point where the leak path goes through the seal plane and repair it. Thus it is
 important to think about all of the possible leak paths between the internal leak source and the
 external leak point.
 NOTE: You can lift the seal plane as an alternative to the procedure to repair the hidden seal
 (PAGEBLOCK 28-11-00/801).

RAM ALL 28-11-00

 D6-37569 Mar 25/2015

 (2) The seal plane is the barrier that keeps the fuel in the fuel tank. When the seal plane has a
 hole, the faying surfaces of all the structure on the other side of the seal plane become wet.
 The wet area becomes larger in all directions from the hole in the seal plane until it touches an
 injection, faying surface, or prepack ("hidden") seal. Fuel leakage usually flows along fillet
 seals until it gets to a point where it can get out of the structure (the external leak point).
 Because there are no seals on the dry side of a seal plane, the fuel will flow out of the structure
 at the point with minimum resistance to fuel. For example, a row of fasteners in a leak path are
 wet, but the leak is shown at only one fastener. If you seal the fastener with the leak, then the
 remaining fastener with the minimum resistance to fuel will have a leak. This process will occur
 again until you repair the seal surface. Make an analysis of the leak path to find out how the
 fuel went from the hole in the seal plane to the external leak point. It is necessary to know the
 tank structure and the sealant to know the leak path fully.

titulo: Fuel Leak Analysis to Find the Cause of the Leaks
procedimento:
(1) These are the causes of most of the leaks in the fuel tank structure:
 (a) Surfaces are prepared incorrectly.
 (b) Sealants are mixed or kept incorrectly.
 (c) Sealants are applied incorrectly.
 (d) Fasteners are loose.
 (e) The fittings or the connections are installed incorrectly.
 (2) This task gives data about the causes of fuel leaks. It also gives general precautions that you
 must obey when you repair leaks.
SUBTASK 28-11-00-288-200

 (1) The surfaces are prepared incorrectly.
 (a) The surfaces must not contain these unwanted materials:
 1) Grease
 2) Metal particles
 3) Hair
 4) Loose paint
 5) Wax
 6) Other unwanted materials.
 (b) These unwanted materials can cause the sealant not to bond correctly.
 SUBTASK 28-11-00-288-239

 (2) The sealants are mixed or kept incorrectly.
 (a) Make sure you mix the correct quantities of the base material and the accelerator
 material.

 accelerator material. Synthetic rubber makes the base for most sealants. The
 manufacturer adds materials to control the strength and cure time. The
 manufacturer also adds materials to make the sealant more flexible and to
 increase the time you can keep it. These materials also make the sealant more
 resistant to fuel.
 1) Obey the instructions from the manufacturer when you mix the sealant.

titulo: Temporary Repair of Leaks Through Self-Sealing Rivets
procedimento:
(1) Self-sealing rivets are frequently used in skin panels in the fuel tank area. If you find a leak at a
 rivet, you must replace the rivet to make a permanent repair. You can make a temporary repair
 if you refer to the Structural Repair Manual to make a permanent repair when you go into the
 tank.
 (2) To make a temporary repair of a self-sealing rivet, use one of these procedures:
 (a) Apply the sealant to a self-sealing rivet with a sealant tool (Figure 816).
 (b) Apply the sealant to a self-sealing rivet with a fuel tank rivet sealing tool, SPL-1762
 (Figure 815).

RAM ALL 28-11-00

 D6-37569 Mar 25/2015

 (c) Install a Click-Patch.
 (3) For applying sealants in the fuel tank structure(s), it is acceptable to use sealant, A50303, as
 an alternative to sealant, A00767, for Class A and B applications:

 (b) sealant, A50110, can be used as an alternative to sealant, A50302.
 (c) sealant, A50153, cannot be used in combination with sealant, A50302, and sealant,
 A50301, cannot be used with sealant, A50110.

titulo: Repair of O-Rings and Rubber Seals

referencias.titulo: WING FUEL TANK ACCESS PANELS - REPAIRS

procedimento:
(1) Leaks can occur around plumbing fittings that you can remove, primary tension bolts, tank
 access doors and fuel system components that go through the fuel tank surfaces. These
 components are sealed by O-rings or by rubber seals. Replace the O-rings or rubber seals
 when they are damaged or have fuel leaks. You must apply the alodine layer to all surfaces of
 the tank structure that are damaged before you install new O-rings or rubber seals.
 (2) O-rings are used to seal these types of components:
 (a) Plumbing fittings that you can remove
 (b) Primary tension bolts
 (c) Access doors for the fuel tanks
 (d) Fuel system components that go through tank walls.
 (3) O-rings are used to seal these components:
 (a) Removable plumbing fittings
 (b) Primary tension bolts
 (c) Access doors for the fuel tank
 (d) Fuel system components that go through fuel tank walls.
 (4) If an O-ring seal has a leak, you must replace it.
 (5) The cast aluminum access doors and the impact-resistant access doors are sealed with a
 rubber seal ring. If the seal on a cast aluminum door has a leak, you must replace the door. If a
 seal on an impact-resistant door has a leak (the seal becomes loose but has no damage), you
 can replace the seal. Refer to this task: "Replacement of the Molded Rubber Door Seal"
 (PAGEBLOCK 28-11-11/801).

 (1) Visually examine all the fuel tubing to make sure it is tightly and correctly attached.
 SUBTASK 28-22-15-826-003

 SUBTASK 28-22-15-216-004

 (3) Visually examine all the fuel tubing for these types of damage and make sure the damage is
 permitted:
 (a) Make an inspection for cracks.
 1) No cracks are permitted.
 (b) Make an inspection for dents (areas that are pushed into the tubing).
 1) All dents must have an area that is large compared to the depth of the dent.
 2) No single dent in the tubing is permitted to decrease the diameter of the tube by
 more than 2.5 percent.
 3) If there are multiple dents, the total dent depth (individual depths added together) in
 any section five times the tube diameter long, must be no more than ten percent of
 the tube diameter.
 4) The dents in the tubing must be farther than one diameter of the tube from the end
 of the tube.
 5) The dents in the tubing must not have an area of more than 0.125 square inches.
 6) If the dent is on the outer part of a bend in the tube, the dent must not have a depth
 of more than .015 inches.
 (c) Do an inspection for nicks.
 1) The nicks in the tubing must have a rounded bottom.
 2) The nicks in the tubing must not have a depth of more than 0.004 inches.
 3) You must remove all the burrs from the nick if there are some burrs.

 28-22-15

 D6-37569 Mar 25/2015

 (d) Do an inspection for fretting.
 1) Fretting must not have a depth of more than 0.004 inches.
 (e) Do an inspection for scoring.
 1) If you find some small scoring, you can make it smooth again, but obey these
 conditions:
 a) The scoring must not be on the outer part of a bend.
 b) You must not remove more than .004 inches of metal.
 (f) Do an inspection for tubes with a cross section that is not fully circular (tubes with
 ovality).
 1) Calculate the percent ovality with this formula:
 percent ovality = [(OD Max - OD Min) ÷ (OD Nominal)] X 100%
 a) OD Max is the maximum outer diameter of the tube
 b) OD Min is the minimum outer diameter of the tube
 c) OD Nominal is the outer diameter of the tube at a position where the tube is
 circular or almost circular.
 2) The percent ovality must not be more than 10% for tubes with a diameter of less
 than 2 inches.
 3) The percent ovality must not be more than 5% for tubes with a diameter of more
 than 2 inches.

procedimento:
(1) There are four different procedures that you can use to defuel the fuel tanks:
 (a) Defuel through the pressure fueling receptacle with the airplane boost pumps and the
 defueling (suction) pump on the refuel truck. This procedure defuels all of the tanks at the
 same time. It is the fastest procedure to defuel the tanks.
 (b) Defuel through the pressure fueling receptacle with the airplane boost pumps only.
 (c) Defuel through the pressure fueling receptacle with the defueling (suction) pump on the
 fuel truck only. Use this procedure only if it is necessary. It is a very slow procedure.
 (d) Defuel through the pressure fueling receptacle with the external power control unit (PCU).
 You must have special ground support equipment to do this procedure.
 (2) With pressure defueling (boost pumps operate), or with pressure and suction together, you can
 defuel all of the fuel tanks to the level of the sump drain valves.
 (a) To completely defuel the center tank, do these steps:
 1) Adjust the airplane attitude to 2 degrees nose up, 0-degree roll if it is possible.
 NOTE: This will minimize the quantity of fuel that remains in the center tank.
 2) Make sure the No. 1 main tank has sufficient capacity available for the fuel to be
 scavenged from the center tank.
 NOTE: The scavenge system will operate for 20 minutes after the boost pump
 switches for the center tank are both in the OFF position.
 3) Operate the forward No. 1 main boost pump to supply the motive flow during fuel
 scavenging.
 (3) You can open and close all of the valves manually if it is necessary. To defuel with the external
 power control unit, you must open and close all of the valves manually.

titulo: Install Jumpers in the New TSD Wire (Safe-Side) Harness
procedimento:
SUBTASK 28-41-35-024-007

 (1) Remove the cover on the connector backshell, and the connector backshell of the J2
 connector on the TSD wire harness.
 SUBTASK 28-41-35-424-008

 (2) Look at and record the J2 pins that are connected (jumper-wired) to pin J2-J inside the
 receptacle.
 NOTE: If pins J2-B and J2-H are the only pins connected to J2-J, these are the nominal
 jumpers, and the new TSD wire harness does not need jumpers installed.
 (a) Remove the nominal jumpers, shipped with the new TSD wire harness (J2-B to J2-H to
 J2-J) with the pin removal tool (M81969/14-02 or equivalent).
 NOTE: Do not remove jumpers between J2-E to J2-G to J2-V.
 (b) Remove the sockets installed in any holes that will need new jumpers.
 SUBTASK 28-41-35-424-015

 (3) Carefully install the jumpers in the locations you recorded with the insertion tool
 (M81969/14-02).
 NOTE: See Figure 401 for the connector pin assignments.
 SUBTASK 28-41-35-424-016

 (4) Cut off the excess pins at the last pin to be installed.
 SUBTASK 28-41-35-424-017

 (5) Install blank connector sockets (MS39029/5-115) and plugs (MS27488-20), or equivalent in
 any unused connector socket locations.
 SUBTASK 28-41-35-394-024

 (6) Apply MIL-PRF-27617F Type III grease into the connector space and backshell cover, to
 prevent moisture.
 SUBTASK 28-41-35-424-018

 (7) Re-install the connector backshell and cover.
 SUBTASK 28-41-35-424-019

 (8) Apply Loctite type C or equivalent on the threads of the screws and the threaded collar and
 tighten immediately.

 (a) Make sure he two values are the same with a tolerance of ±7°F (±4 °C).

procedimento:
(1) Use this procedure to find the total internal leakage of the A or B hydraulic system.
 (2) You must find the changes in the flow of hydraulic fluid (during different conditions of operation)
 to find the internal leakage rate for each part. There are three procedures to measure the flow:
 the ammeter procedure, the flowmeter procedure, and the amp-clamp and multimeter
 procedure.
 NOTE: Do not operate the EDP or EMDP with the hydraulic service cart return and pressure
 lines connected. This may prevent the pumps from receiving enough hydraulic fluid
 from their respective reservoirs and cavitate the pump.
 (a) To use the ammeter procedure, you connect an ammeter in series with one phase of the
 motor on the electric motor-driven pump (EMDP). To find the flow you measure the
 current subtract the basic current and use Figure 603 to change it to a flow.
 (b) To use the flowmeter procedure, you install a flowmeter on a hydraulic service cart and
 read the flow from it.
 (c) To use the amp-clamp and multimeter procedure, you put the amp-clamp adapter around
 one of the wires connected to a relay for the EMDP. You then read the current on the
 multimeter (that is connected to the amp-clamp adapter) subtract the basic current and
 use Figure 603 to get the flow. One person can do this procedure from the Control Cabin.
 (3) When you read the ammeter, make a record of the value to the nearest 0.1 ampere. Use
 Figure 603 to change current to flow.
 (4) When you read the flowmeter, make a record of the value to the nearest 100 cc/minute.

procedimento:
(1) Use this procedure to find the general internal condition of the standby hydraulic system.
 (2) To find the internal leakage of the standby system you will measure the flow (from the standby
 EMDP) before and after the standby rudder actuator is in operation. There are three
 procedures to measure the flow from the standby EMDP: the ammeter procedure, the
 flowmeter procedure, and the amp-clamp and multimeter procedure.
 NOTE: The standby rudder actuator is the only actuator that gets power only from the standby
 EMDP. Thus, it is the only actuator that you must examine in this task
 (a) To use the ammeter procedure, you connect an ammeter in series with one phase of the
 motor on the standby EMDP. To find the flow you measure the current and use
 Figure 608 to change it to a flow.
 (b) To use the flowmeter procedure, you install a flowmeter at the outlet of the standby
 EMDP and read the flow from it.
 (c) To use the amp-clamp and multimeter procedure, you put the amp-clamp adapter around
 one of the wires connected to a circuit breaker for the standby EMDP. You then read the
 current on the multimeter (that is connected to the amp-clamp adapter) and use
 Figure 608 to get the flow. One person can do this procedure from the Control Cabin.
 NOTE: You can also use one of the three load wires connected to standby hydraulic
 pump relay, R68, to put the amp-clamp adapter around.

titulo: Pressurize the A, B, or Standby Hydraulic System

referencias.titulo: HYDRAULIC SYSTEMS A, B, AND STANDBY - DESCRIPTION

procedimento:
(1) Hydraulic systems A and B are almost the same, thus the same procedure is used for the two
 systems. The standby hydraulic system has a different procedure.
 (2) If you pressurize the A hydraulic system, these parts will get hydraulic power:
 (a) The ground spoilers (0, 1, 4, 5, 8, 9)
 (b) Through the alternate (brake) source selector valve (alternate source)
 1) The alternate brakes
 (c) The left thrust reverser (primary source)
 (d) The landing gear transfer valve (primary source landing gear operation)
 (e) Through the system A flight control module
 1) The flight spoilers (3, 6)
 2) The lower aileron power control unit
 3) The right auto-pilot actuator
 4) The rudder
 5) The left elevator power control unit
 6) The lower auto-pilot actuator
 7) The left elevator feel
 (3) If you pressurize the B hydraulic system, these parts will get hydraulic power:
 (a) The leading edge flaps and slats
 (b) The trailing edge flaps
 (c) The primary brakes
 (d) The right thrust reverser (primary source)
 (e) The landing gear transfer valve (alternate source landing gear operation)
 (f) Through the system B flight control module
 1) The flight spoilers (2, 7)
 2) The upper aileron power control unit
 3) The left auto-pilot actuator
 4) The rudder
 5) The right elevator power control unit
 6) The upper auto-pilot actuator
 7) The right elevator feel
 (4) If you pressurize the standby hydraulic system, these parts will get hydraulic power.

procedimento:
(1) This procedure flushes the hydraulic system after you replace a defective hydraulic pump.
 (2) If the airplane experiences repeated failures of a pump at one location, there may be debris in
 the case drain line, case drain hose or case drain hose quick-disconnect that cannot be
 flushed by accomplishing this procedure. Careful examination, cleaning, or replacement of the
 case drain hose or quick-disconnect may be required.
 (3) If metal contamination from a damaged pump is found when you flush the hydraulic system,
 then it is recommended to do these steps:
 NOTE: Operator experience shows that a new filter can become plugged by debris that
 remains in the hydraulic system after a mechanical failure. A plugged filter can cause
 hydraulic fluid to bypass the filter element and allow debris to circulate in the system.
 Debris that bypasses the filter can cause a premature failure of a new hydraulic pump.
 (a) Replace the case drain filter element again, at the first scheduled maintenance
 opportunity following one week of normal operation.
 (b) Replace all the filter elements in the system at the first scheduled maintenance
 opportunity following two months of normal operation.
 (4) If there is chemical contamination in the hydraulic fluid, the hydraulic fluid and the filter
 elements must be replaced (PAGEBLOCK 29-00-00/201).
 (5) When you work on parts from the hydraulic system, flush them only with BMS 3-11 hydraulic
 fluid. This keeps contamination out of the hydraulic system.

 (2) Look for metal contamination in the pressure filter for the EMDP (PAGEBLOCK 29-15-71/201).
 If you find metal contamination, do these steps:
 (a) Flush the hydraulic lines between the pressure filter and the EMDP.
 (b) Replace the pressure filter element (PAGEBLOCK 29-15-71/201).
 (c) If you find a small quantity of metal particles that have equal dimensions, then replace the
 filter and do an operational test of the pump (PAGEBLOCK 29-15-00/501). Examine the
 filter again at the scheduled filter change interval.
 NOTE: It is not necessary to replace a pump if the quantity of metal particles is small and
 they have equal dimensions. The filter can have more particles during initial
 operation of a new pump while mating parts wear away small surface defects. It
 is not necessary to replace the pump if more small particles are found at the next
 filter change after installation of a new pump.
 (d) If you find a large quantity of small metal particles, large metal particles that are not of
 equal dimensions, or a large quantity of steel particles, then replace the pump at the next
 maintenance opportunity (PAGEBLOCK 29-15-21/401 or PAGEBLOCK 29-15-22/401).
 NOTE: A large quantity of small metal particles, of large metal particles that are not of
 equal dimensions, can be an indication of an unsatisfactory pump. The particles
 are usually bronze mixed with a small quantity of steel. A large quantity of steel
 particles is an indication of unsatisfactorily worn bearings.
 (e) Write down the results of the filter inspection and give them to the pump overhaul facility.
 NOTE: The filter inspection results can be used as an aid to find the condition of the
 pump. A pump with an unsatisfactory bearing can pass the functional test and be
 returned to service with no fault found. Giving the filter inspection data to the
 overhaul facility can prevent the return of an unsatisfactory pump to service.

titulo: Operational Test - Control Cabin Window Anti-Icing System
procedimento:
(1) This test makes sure the control cabin window anti-icing system provides heat to the front,
 side, number 4, and number 5 windows.
SUBTASK 30-41-00-845-065

 (1) Use an infared thermometer, a FLUKE Model 189 multimeter or other temperature indicating
 device near each window temperature sensor to measure the window temperature.
 SUBTASK 30-41-00-885-064

 (2) If the window temperature is greater than 110 degrees F (43 degrees C), then cool the window.
 NOTE: The window can be cooled with cool water or by providing shade from the sun.
 SUBTASK 30-41-00-865-066

 (3) One switch at a time, put the WINDOW HEAT switches on the Window and Pitot Heat Module
 to the ON position.
 (a) Make sure the corresponding ON light on the window and pitot heat modules comes on.
 NOTE: It can take up to 15 seconds for the light to come on.
 (b) Make sure both Master Caution lights are off.
 SUBTASK 30-41-00-215-067

 (4) Wait for the windows to heat up.
 (a) Make sure the front and side windows stabilize at 90 to 120 degrees F (32 to 49 degrees
 C).
 NOTE: It can take up to 4 minutes for the window temperature to stabilize.
 (b) Make sure the number 4 and number 5 windows heat up to more than 90 degrees F (32
 degrees C) but less than 125 degrees F (52 degrees C).
 SUBTASK 30-41-00-865-068

 (5) Put the WINDOW HEAT TEST OVHT/PWR switch to the OVHT position for 1 second.

 (e) Make sure the ON lights go off in less than 70 seconds.

procedimento:
SUBTASK 30-41-11-865-005

 (1) Supply electrical power (PAGEBLOCK 24-22-00/201).

 2) 28 VDC PITOT STATIC INDICATION - F/O
 SUBTASK 30-41-11-715-002

 (3) Make sure that the window heat indicator light operates:
 (a) Push the applicable window heat ON light on the WINDOW HEAT CONTROL MODULE.
 (b) Make sure that the ON light comes on.

 (4) Do this test of the window heat control unit:

 switch.

 OVERHEAT light comes on.

 4) Make sure that the window heat ON light comes on.

procedimento:
(1) The No. 1, No. 2, No. 4, and No. 5 windows have a layer of material on them that transmits
 electricity. This layer has an electrical resistance. With time the electrical resistance of this
 layer increases.

titulo: Anti-Ice Operation with 115 Volts AC on the Ground
procedimento:
(1) Usually 28 volt AC is used to remove the ice from the drain mast while the airplane is on the
 ground. The 115 volt AC is usually used while the airplane is in the air.
 (2) Do not use this task unless the 28 volt system will not remove the ice from the drain mast(s).
 This task can be used as an equivalent to airborne systems that melt the ice in the drain
 mast(s).
SUBTASK 30-71-00-862-008

 (1) Supply electrical power (PAGEBLOCK 24-22-00/201).
 SUBTASK 30-71-00-862-010

 CAUTION: BE CAREFUL WHEN YOU USE THE 115 VOLT SYSTEM TO MELT THE ICE IN THE
 DRAIN MAST ON THE GROUND. THE 115 VOLT ELECTRICAL POWER CAN CAUSE
 THE DRAIN MAST TO BECOME TOO HOT. THE HEAT CAN CAUSE DAMAGE TO
 THE DRAIN MAST.
 (2) Do these steps to supply the 115 volt electrical power to the Anti-Ice system:
 (a) Set the APU GENERATOR 1 AND 2 switches on the P5-4 panel to ON.
 (b) Open this circuit breaker on the P6-12 panel:
 1) EXTERNAL BUS PROTECTION
 (c) Open this access door for the forward nose compartment:
 Number Name/Location
 1103 Forward Access Door
 (d) Push the AIR SENSING test switch on the E11 landing gear logic shelf.
 SUBTASK 30-71-00-862-009

 (3) As soon as the ice is melted, do these steps to remove the 115 volt power from the Anti-Ice
 system:
 (a) Release the AIR SENSING test switch on the E11 landing gear logic shelf.
 (b) Close this circuit breaker on the P6-12 panel:
 1) EXTERNAL BUS PROTECTION
 (c) Set the APU GENERATOR 1 AND 2 switches on the P5-4 panel to OFF.
 SUBTASK 30-71-00-862-005

 (4) Remove electrical power (PAGEBLOCK 24-22-00/201).
 SUBTASK 30-71-00-412-007

 Number Name/Location
 1103 Forward Access Door

titulo: Copy the data from the FDR with SFIM Ground Support Equipment (GSE)
procedimento:
(1) The SFIM Ground Support Equipment (GSE) is used to copy data from the SFIM solid state
 flight data recorder (FDR). The GSE can be used while the FDR is installed in the airplane.
 The GSE is connected to the ATE connector of the FDR front panel.
SUBTASK 31-24-00-862-135

 (1) Enter SSFDR from the C: > prompt.
 SUBTASK 31-24-00-862-136

 (2) Push the enter key.
 (a) Select DATA RETRIEVAL FROM SSFDR/GSE from the menu.
 NOTE: Use the arrow keys to move up, down, right and left of the menu, then push the
 enter key to make a selection.
 (b) Select DOWNLOAD SSFDR DATA MEMORY.
 NOTE: The GSE will start to make a copy of the flight data from the FDR. The process
 will take approximately 2 minutes.
 (c) Enter the serial number of the FDR.
 NOTE: The GSE will identify the download files as FDRxxx. COD and FDRxxxx. IDT.
 Where xxxx is the serial number of the FDR.
 (d) Select the START command.
 NOTE: If there is not enough memory on the diskette, the GSE will abort the copy
 operation.
 (e) If the equipment, COM-1810 aborts the copy command, do this step:
 1) Delete files.
 NOTE: GSE will ask for confirmation when it deletes files with the name of
 FDRxxxx. COD or FDRxxxx. IDT. When there is sufficient memory the GSE
 will start the download process.
 (f) Make sure DOWNLOAD DATA IN PROGRESS is shown on the equipment, COM-1810
 display.
 NOTE: The download takes approximately 2 minutes.
 (g) Make sure DOWNLOAD DATA COMPLETE shows on the display when the equipment,
 COM-1810 completes the download.
 (h) Push any key.
 SUBTASK 31-24-00-862-123

 (3) Set the TEST--NORMAL switch to the NORMAL position.
 SUBTASK 31-24-00-822-121

(1) The takeoff warning system has these switches:
 (a) Two thrust lever operated warning switches

 serviceable only when the airplane is on the ground.

 (5) When you move one of the thrust levers forward to the takeoff position, the warning system
 operates.

 configuration, the intermittent horn operates.

 TEST switch (S785), installed on the E3-1 shelf.

3. Nose Gear Steering Lockout Pin - Removal/Installation
 (Figure 202 )

 A. Tools/Equipment
 NOTE: When more than one tool part number is listed under the same "Reference" number, the
 tools shown are alternates to each other within the same airplane series. Tool part numbers
 that are replaced or non-procurable are preceded by "Opt:", which stands for Optional.
 Reference Description
 SPL-9807 Ground Lock Assy - Nose Wheel Steering - 737-200,300,400,500 *
 Flyaway Eqpt *
 737-400HGW, -500
 Part #: F72735-13 Supplier: 81205
 B. Procedure - Nose Gear Steering Lockout Pin Installation
 SUBTASK 32-00-01-422-005

 (1) Install the nose wheel steering ground lock, SPL-9807:
 (a) Push the knob on the nose gear steering depressurization valve and hold it in the
 depressed position.
 (b) Push the button on the lockout pin and fully insert the pin in the hole in the side of then
 depressurization valve.

procedimento:
(1) The apex joint inspection is important to make sure the shimmy damper functions properly and

 effectiveness is reduced.
SUBTASK 32-11-00-220-001

 (1) Using a feeler gauge, STD-405, examine the upper and lower torsion link end play. Refer to
 Figure 32-11-51-990-802 locations (2) and (4).

 links or shim gap per Figure 32-11-51-990-802, flagnote 6.

 SUBTASK 32-11-00-820-002

 flagnote 8 (PAGEBLOCK 32-11-51/601).

 completed.

 links (PAGEBLOCK 32-11-51/401).

 Reference Title

 217 Right Main Wheel Well
 C. Adjust the Main Gear Damper
 SUBTASK 32-11-81-225-003

 (1) Measure the distance from the end of the cap of the damper housing to the head of the
 damper piston (Figure 501).
 NOTE: Under normal condition the damper piston head position can be outside the
 dimensions shown in (Figure 501). The location of the piston is important when the
 torque on the apex nut is set in the steps that follow.
 SUBTASK 32-11-81-225-004

 (2) If the head of the damper piston is not within the dimension shown in Figure 501, do the steps
 that follow:
 (a) Lift the main landing gear on an axle jack (PAGEBLOCK 07-11-31/201).
 (b) Use a length of wood to turn the wheels to move the piston head in or out of the shimmy
 damper housing.
 (c) Turn the wheels until the piston head is within the dimension shown in (Figure 501).
 SUBTASK 32-11-81-820-001

 (3) Do these steps to adjust the apex nut:
 (a) Remove the lockwire from the lockbolt to the checknut.
 (b) Remove the lockbolt and tighten the apex nut of the torsion link to 400 in-lb (45.2 Nm) to
 500 in-lb (56.5 Nm).
 (c) Loosen the apex nut to zero torque.
 (d) Tighten the apex nut to 50 in-lb (5.6 Nm) to 150 in-lb (16.9 Nm) until the next available
 hole in the apex nut aligns with a hole in the lockwasher.
 (e) Install the lockbolt, the washer, the nut in the apex nut and the lockwasher.
 (f) Tighten the checknut to 50 in-lb (5.6 Nm) to 100 in-lb (11.3 Nm).
 (g) Install the lockwire from the lockbolt to the checknut.
 SUBTASK 32-11-81-865-023

 (4) Put the Airplane Back to its Usual Condition.

 (Figure 803)

 A. Procedure to Repair the Axle Sleeves of the Main Landing Gear
 SUBTASK 32-11-85-218-016

 (1) Do a check on the wear limits of the bearing boss.
 (a) Examine the diameters of the inboard and the outboard bearing boss for worn areas as
 shown on (Figure 802).
 NOTE: If worn areas on the bearing boss is more than the specified wear limits and the
 clearance between the bearing and the boss is more than 0.006 inch, you must
 remove the axle sleeve and replace or rework (Ref 32-11-11, OHM).
 If worn areas on the bearing boss is more than the specified wear limits and the
 clearance between the bearing and the boss is not more than 0.006 inch, the
 axle sleeves can continue to be in service for 65 hours flying time before removal
 for replacement or repair (Ref 32-11-11, OHM).
 SUBTASK 32-11-85-358-017

 (2) Repair the local damage between the bearing surfaces.
 (a) Remove the sharp edges and make a smooth finish on the damage to a 0.50 inch radius.

 32-41-41

 (a) Brake pistons
 (b) brake housing ports

 (d) bleed ports
 SUBTASK 32-41-41-796-009

 brakes are being applied, repair the leak(s) or replace the brake prior to dispatch.
 SUBTASK 32-41-41-796-037

 (7) Brakes with leaks below these limits must be rechecked prior to each flight, and should be
 repaired or replaced at the next opportunity that manpower and material allow.

 component maintenance manual if it is suspected that a brake has been exposed to significant

 charred residue, or heavy smoke after landing.

 (1) Examine the brake assembly for these types of damage:
 (a) Cracks that you can see.

 (e) Parts that are loose.

 (2) Do these steps to make sure that the components that apply force to the brake rotors and

 (d) Make sure that the pressure plate goes back to the initial position each time that you
 release the brake.
 (e) Do this additional check to make sure that the pressure plate will operate properly:
 1) Make sure that the brake pedals are released and pressure is released from the
 brake.

 and push or pull on them to move the wear plate.
 3) Move the pressure plate back in contact with the adjacent rotor disc.
 NOTE: Do not use a tool to apply force to the pressure plate to make it move.
 4) Look at the piston side of the plate and make sure that the pressure plate drive lugs
 are in their correct position.

 (a) Grasp the cap assembly and pull directly out to retract the cap assembly locking pins.

 assembly into the base assembly. Therefore, the shaft will not actuate the
 switches and the lamps will fail to contact the energized pins in the
 mounting base.
 (d) Insert the cap assembly into the mounting base. Push with a firm continuous action until
 the cap assembly bottoms out in the base assembly. The cap assembly should collapse
 and the locking pins should engage the base assembly.

 to prematurely release and cause the unit to jam.

(1) These general instructions apply to the pitot-static system leak test.
 (a) The rate of the applied vacuum to a static system must be 5000 feet or less for each
 minute.
 (b) The release of the vacuum from a static system must be 5000 feet or less for each
 minute.
 (c) The rate of the applied pressure to a pitot system must be 300 knots or less for each
 minute.
 (d) The release of pressure from a pitot system must be 300 knots or less for each minute.
 (e) Absolute pressure in the pitot system must be equal or more than the pressure in the
 static system.
 (f) The differential pressure between the pitot and static systems must not be larger than
 10.00 inches of mercury.
 (g) The absolute pressure applied to a static system must not be more than ambient
 pressure when an instrument is connected to that static system.
 (h) The pressure in a static system must not be more than 32.10 inches of mercury.
 (i) Do not connect or disconnect equipment or indicators when you apply pressure or a
 vacuum to the pitot-static system.
 (j) Remove the drain fitting caps during the leak test.
 (k) Make sure that the pitot-static probe heat is off during the test.
 (l) Make sure that the autopilot system is off during the test.
 WARNING: MAKE SURE THE ATC TRANSPONDERS ARE NOT IN AN ALTITUDE MODE
 WHEN YOU SIMULATE ALTITUDE. IF YOU DO NOT, YOU CAN
 ACCIDENTALLY CAUSE FALSE TCAS TARGETS.
 (m) Make sure the ATC transponders are not in an altitude reporting mode.

titulo: Air Data System - Operational Test (For Honeywell ADCs P/N HG480B42 and HG480B43)
procedimento:
(1) This is the air data system operational test for the Honeywell Air Data Computer (ADC), part
 numbers HG480B42 and HG480B43.
 (2) The ADS operational test is a BITE test. The test operates from the controls on the front panel
 of the ADC. During the test, stable outputs are sent to the air data instruments and are
 monitored. The test makes sure of the conditions that follow:
 (a) The ADC electronics operate correctly.
 (b) The interface and warning system between the computer and instruments operate
 correctly.
 (c) The instruments operate when signals are sent to them.

procedimento:
(1) This procedure tells you how to install software in the EFIS SG.
 (a) The SG must contain this piece of software:
 1) Operational Program Software (OPS)
 (2) A Portable Data Loader (PDL) is necessary for this procedure.
 (3) A Tray Adapter is necessary for this procedure.
 (4) The airplane must be on the ground with the engines off before you can install the software.
SUBTASK 34-22-41-010-002

 (1) Open this access panel:
 Number Name/Location
 1201 Electronic Equipment Access Door
 SUBTASK 34-22-41-862-036

 (2) Do this task: Supply Electrical Power (PAGEBLOCK 24-22-00/201).
 SUBTASK 34-22-41-472-042

 (3) Use a PDL and Tray Adapter to install software in the SG.
 NOTE: You must know the correct software part number for the SG. For the SG to be an
 approved installation, you must install the software with the correct part number. You
 can do a check of the SG software part number with the EFIS Symbol Generator Test
 (PAGEBLOCK 34-22-41/401).
 SUBTASK 34-22-41-842-038

 (4) Do these steps to prepare for the software installation:
 (a) Set the EFI Transfer Switch on the pilots' overhead panel to NORMAL.
 (b) Open these circuit breakers and attach DO-NOT-CLOSE tags:
 1) On the circuit breaker panel, P18-2
 a) C01110, EFIS SYMBOL GENERATOR - LEFT
 2) On the circuit breaker panel, P6-1
 a) C01114, EFIS SYMBOL GENERATOR - RIGHT
 (c) Remove the EFIS SYMBOL GENERATOR - LEFT. Do this task: EFIS Symbol Generator
 Removal (PAGEBLOCK 34-22-41/401).
 (d) Install the Tray Adapter in the EFIS SYMBOL GENERATOR - LEFT tray. Make sure that
 the Tray Adapter is fully seated in the tray.
 (e) Install the EFIS SYMBOL GENERATOR - LEFT in the Tray Adapter. Make sure that the
 SG is fully seated in the Tray Adapter.
 (f) Set the power switch on the PDL to OFF.
 (g) Connect the interface cable from the PDL to the Tray Adapter.
 (h) Remove the DO-NOT-CLOSE tag and close this circuit breaker:
 1) On the circuit breaker panel, P18-2
 a) C01110, EFIS SYMBOL GENERATOR - LEFT
 SUBTASK 34-22-41-472-039

 (5) Do these steps to install the software:
 NOTE: Refer to the supplier's instructions for more information on how to use the PDL.
 (a) Set the power switch on the PDL to ON. The PDL will do a self-test.
 (b) Wait for the PDL self-test to stop.
 (c) Put the correct disk in the disk drive. The PDL will read the disk and show that it is ready.
 The data loading will start.

 NOTE: Ferromagnetic parts installed near the standby compass can cause compass heading
 errors. Make sure no ferromagnetic parts are near the captain's and the first officer's window
 frames. If found, replace the parts with non-magnetic, corrosion-resistant steel (CRES)
 parts.
 SUBTASK 34-24-00-582-032

 (1) Tow the airplane to the compass swing area (PAGEBLOCK 09-10-00/201).
 NOTE: The compass swing area must be a level area with a smooth surface. It must be
 sufficiently strong to hold the weight of the airplane. The area must be large enough to
 tow or taxi the airplane. Make sure all vehicles other than the tow vehicle are not less
 than 220 feet from the airplane.
 The horizontal component of the earth's magnetic field must be constant (±1 degree)
 in the test area. Measure the horizontal component if magnetic material (such as a
 new building) is less than 600 feet from the compass rose. Do not use the compass
 rose if the horizontal component is not constant (±1 degree).

(1) The operational test has these parts:
 (a) The prepare for a weather radar system operational test.
 (b) The weather radar system self test.
 (c) The test of the antenna TILT control on the WXR control panel.
 (2) The self-test uses the mode selector switch on the WXR control panel in the TEST mode. In
 the TEST mode, the self-test circuits monitor the performance of the weather radar system.
 (3) The weather radar control panel is referred to as the WXR control panel.
 (4) During the self test the weather radar system operates as follows:
 (a) It makes a test pattern which finds most system failures without test equipment.
 (b) The receiver/transmitter operates for 4 seconds.
 (c) A special test pattern is made on the EHSIs.
NOTE: A test pattern, which appears distorted along a radial line (segmented test pattern) during
 the first sweep of the weather radar is normal. An abnormal condition occurs if the above
 test pattern continues after the second full sweep.

titulo: Verify the Terrain Database Part Number
procedimento:
(1) This task provides instructions to verify the terrain database part number. The GPWC level 3
 self-test provides aural annunciations of the current configuration that include the terrain
 database part number.
 (2) The GPWC level 3 self-test can only be activated when the airplane is on the ground.
SUBTASK 34-42-03-862-010

 (1) Make sure the ground proximity warning system (GPWS) is operational
 (PAGEBLOCK 34-42-03/501).
 SUBTASK 34-42-03-862-011

 (2) Make sure the COMPUTER OK light on the front panel of the GPWC is on and the other lights
 are off.
 SUBTASK 34-42-03-862-012

 (3) Open the door on the front panel of the GPWC.
 SUBTASK 34-42-03-862-020

 (4) Plug the headphone, STD-1390 into the headphone jack of the GPWC.
 SUBTASK 34-42-03-862-013

 (5) Make sure there is no card in the card slot of the GPWC.
 SUBTASK 34-42-03-702-017

 (6) Do these steps to do the level 3 self-test of the GPWC:
 NOTE: The GPWC self-test has six levels that operate in sequence. The level 3 self-test will
 occur after the level 2 self-test.
 (a) Push the self-test switch on the GPWC for one second.
 (b) After the level 1 self-test starts, push the self-test switch for one second to go to the level
 2 self-test.
 (c) After the level 2 self-test starts, wait until the PRESS TO CONTINUE annunciation
 occurs, then push the self-test switch for one second to go to the level 3 self-test.

RAM ALL; AIRPLANES WITH ENHANCED GPWS
 34-42-03

 D6-37569 Mar 25/2015

 (d) You will hear a sequence of the configuration annunciations for the GPWS over the
 headphone.
 1) Make sure you hear the terrain database part number after the TERRAIN
 DATABASE VERSION annunciation.
 NOTE: There are several configuration annunciations in the level 3 self-test. To
 advance to the terrain database part number annunciation, you need to
 push the self-test switch after each annunciation.
 (e) Record the terrain database part number.
 (f) After you hear the terrain database part number, continue to push the self-test switch until
 you hear the PRESS TO CONTINUE annunciation.
 NOTE: After the PRESS TO CONTINUE annunciates, the level 3 self-test is complete. If
 you do not push the self-test switch again, the self-test sequence will stop.
 (g) If your airline maintains a terrain database version requirement, make sure the terrain
 database version is correct.
 1) If the part number or version is not correct, then do this task: Load the Terrain
 Database (PAGEBLOCK 34-42-03/201).

titulo: Radio Altitude Simulation (TRT Ramp Test Unit SIM 530)
procedimento:
(1) Use this procedure with TRT ERT-530(A) receiver/transmitters (R/Ts) that have dc (analog) or
 digital radio altitude output.
 (2) One test connector and three cables are available to operate the test set with one, two, or
 three R/Ts.
 (3) The test has two procedures:
 (a) Radio Altitude Ramp-down
 (b) Manually Simulated Radio Altitude
 (4) Do these procedures in sequence to make sure equipment setup and operation are correct.
SUBTASK 34-48-02-720-003

 (1) Make a check of the radio altimeter test set, COM-1922 ramp-down program:
 (a) Set these controls on the radio altimeter test set, COM-1922:
 1) Push and release the REMOTE TEST-RA1 HOLD button.
 2) Make sure the middle switch on the left side of the radio altimeter test set,
 COM-1922 is in the REMOTE TEST position.
 3) Put the VOLTS/FAULT CODE/FEET switch in the BUS 1 position.
 4) Put the RA DISPLAY in the 1 position.
 NOTE: This sets the test unit to do a test of the R/T connected to the cable
 connector RA1.
 5) Set the thumbwheels for the REMOTE TEST ALTITUDE to give a ramp-down from
 +4000 feet to -20 feet.
 a) Set the UPPER (FEET) wheels to 4000.
 b) Set the SLOPE (FEET/SECOND) wheels to 20.
 c) Set the LOWER (FEET) wheels to -0020.
 6) Make sure the D/A OUTPUT LEDs show +4000.

RAM ALL 34-48-02

 D6-37569 Mar 25/2015

 (b) Push and release the REMOTE TEST-START button to start the ramp-down program.
 NOTE: The ramp-down can be stopped or continued at altitudes between +4000 feet
 and -20 feet. To do this, push the REMOTE TEST-RA1 HOLD button again.
 (c) Look for these conditions on the applicable EADI radio altitude display.
 1) The display is blank for approximately 75 seconds after you push the REMOTE
 TEST-START button.
 2) The display then shows 2500 (white numerals) and decreases at 20 fps (feet per
 second).
 3) After approximately 98 seconds, at 600 feet, the letters DH will flash (amber) for
 three seconds on the captain's PFD only.
 4) The radio altitude continues to decrease to the stop altitude of -20 feet.
 (d) If it is necessary to do the previous +4000 to -20 foot cycle again, push and release the
 REMOTE TEST-START button.

titulo: System Test - ATC System (With the TIC T-48 or T-49 Test Set)
procedimento:
(1) This system test is a more complete check of the ATC system. The system test first does the
 ATC - Operational Test. Then it uses ground test equipment to examine the left and right ATC
 systems.
 (2) This system test uses the T-48/-49 ramp test set, COM-10730 to test the functionality of the
 ATC transponder. The test set can do all the tests automatically or each test individually. Each
 test shows on the test set as it is done. If a test has failed, the test sequence will stop and a
 failed message shows. All data will show at the end of the test if the test is successful.
 (3) Operation with the antenna coupler, TAP-115, TAP 118, or TAP 125 used with the applicable
 test set, is necessary when the test to do a check of the output power, receiver, sensitivity and
 radio frequency. For mode S diversity channel isolation check, the TAP 125 is necessary.

titulo: System Test - ATC System (With the TIC TR-220 Test Set)
procedimento:
(1) This system test is a full check of the ATC system. The system test first does the ATC
 operational test and then uses the TR-220 ramp test set, COM-10728 to examine the left and
 right ATC systems.
 (2) The TR-220 Test Set is capable of testing ATCRBS Mode A, Mode C and Mode S
 transponders. The operator can select between an Automatic series of tests and a Manual
 series of tests. The Test Set will determine the correct set of tests, either Mode A/C or Mode S
 upon receiving the transponder RF signal. The TR-220 can also test Mode S Transponders
 with Enhanced Surveillance (EHS) capabilities.
 (3) The test set can do all of the tests automatically except the IDENT BUTTON CHECK. You
 must do this test manually with the test set. If a test has failed, the automatic test sequence will
 stop and a failed message will show. At the end of the automatic test all data will show.
 (4) You can manually do each test individually. Push the AUTO/TEST/MANUAL switch to the
 MANUAL position to do each test individually. The test results will show after each test is done.
 After each test is completed, you must toggle the MANUAL switch to advance to the next test
 in the series.
 (5) Operation with the antenna coupler TAP-200 used with the test set, reduces Radio Frequency
 emissions from the transponder being tested.
 It is not necessary to use the coupler to perform these tests.
 (6) If it is necessary to simulate the aircraft at altitude, notify the local ATC that the transponder
 testing is in progress.

titulo: System Test - ATC System (With the ATC-601 Test Set)
procedimento:
(1) This system test is a more complete check of the ATC system. The system test first does the
 ATC - Operational Test, then it uses ground test equipment to examine the left and right ATC
 systems.
 (2) The ATC-601 can test ATCRBS Mode A, Mode C and Mode S transponders. ATC-601 test sets
 with software version 3.0 or higher can also test Mode S Transponders with Enhanced
 Surveillance (ELS, EHS and ES) capabilities.
 (3) The ATC-601 Series ramp test set, COM-4113 test set uses thirty-nine (39) different tests to
 check the functionality of the ATC transponder. All thirty-nine (39) tests can be run
 automatically in the AUTO mode, or individually in the single test mode.
 (4) In the AUTO mode, the test set will determine the correct set of tests, either Mode A/C or Mode
 S upon receiving the transponder RF signal, and will automatically run the tests.
 (5) The details of individual tests conducted during the AUTO TEST are stored in memory and
 may be reviewed by using the SELECT keys. The PASSED/FAILED indication is shown on top
 of the page.
 (6) A passed Auto Test complies with the FAR Part 43 Appendix F test requirements.
 (7) If a test section fails or more data is necessary, use the Single Test Sequence. This lets the
 user do each test individually or see the test results.
 (8) To do a single test, use the SELECT keys to get to the desired test and push the RUN/STOP
 key. The test will continue until the RUN/STOP key is pushed again.
 (9) Results from the last test done, Auto Test or Single Test, show on the display.

 Aerospace, Scott and AvOx oxygen generators.

 case [7].
 (d) Carefully move the release pin [6] and the firing pin [8] away from the firing pin spring
 case [7] with the pin retraction pliers [9]. Do not release the firing pin retraction pliers.
 1) If needed, use the pin retraction pliers [9] to put pressure on the release pin [6] to
 keep the release pin engaged with the firing pin [8] during this next step.

 the firing pin that is nearest the firing pin spring case [7]. Make sure that the safety pin [5]
 is between the firing pin [8] and the firing pin spring case [7].

 firing pin [8].

2. Duct Cleaning
 A. Clean the Ducts
 SUBTASK 36-19-15-117-003

 (1) If the ducts are touched with the fire-resistant hydraulic fluid, clean the ducts (SOPM 20-30-03,
 Section 8, Manual Cleaning).
 SUBTASK 36-19-15-117-004

 (2) Titanium ducts that require the removal of hydraulic fluid contamination while installed on the
 airplane may be cleaned as follows:
 (a) Clean the duct with the use solvents such as cold alkaline, solvent emulsion, and foam
 cleaners (SOPM 20-30-03, Section 8, Manual Cleaning).
 (b) Soak ducts with thick hydraulic fluid residues with alkaline solvent for 20 to 40 minutes,
 then scrape it off the duct with a soft piece of wood (tongue depressor).
 NOTE: Do not remove hydraulic fluid residues on titanium ducts with power wire brush or
 abrasive air blast materials. Aluminized steel wool or scotch brite pads may be
 used. The ducts may be stained as many times as you want after it has been
 cleaned and provided that all the hydraulic fluid residues has been removed and
 the surface of the duct is smooth.
 SUBTASK 36-19-15-377-004

 (3) After you clean the ducts, you can paint them with BMS 10-82 low emissitivity gold coating
 (SOPM 20-44-01) or B-2000 high temperature coating (SOPM 20-41-01, SRF-14.87) to
 provide a protective coating for the duct.
 NOTE: B-2000 high temperature coating may be applied over worn or scarred BMS 10-82
 gold coating or to bare titanium ducting.

2. Duct Repair
 (Figure 801)

 A. Repair the ducts with smooth dents
 SUBTASK 36-19-15-358-002

 (1) Do one of the steps that follow to repair the ducts with smooth dents:
 NOTE: It is not necessary to repair the duct if the smooth dent does not limit the air flow
 through the duct.
 (a) You can pull a ball mandrel through the area of the duct that has the dent.
 (b) You can use an expansion device that is hydraulically or mechanically operated to
 remove the dent.
 (c) You can use hydrostatic pressure in the duct while you lightly hit the edge of the dent with
 a hammer that is not metal.
 NOTE: Be careful you do not use a pressure that is more than the pressure permitted for
 the system.
 SUBTASK 36-19-15-358-003

 (2) Do these steps to repair the ducts that have scratches, gouges and corrosion:
 (a) It is not necessary to repair the duct if the scratch, gouge or corrosion is less than 10% of
 the duct wall thickness.
 NOTE: The change from the base metal thickness must be smooth and rounded. The
 bottom of the scratch, gouge or corrosion must be smooth and rounded also.
 (b) Sharp scratches, gouges and corrosions can be repaired. You can remove some of the
 adjacent metal surface to make the scratch, gouge or corrosion smooth. You can do this
 if you have the conditions that follow:
 1) The thickness of the duct wall at the scratch, gouge or corrosion must be a
 minimum of 90% of the initial thickness.
 2) The surface of the duct must not be rougher than 40 RMS.
 3) The slope of the area must not be more than 1 to 10.
 4) The internal and external radii of the area must be not less than 0.12 inches.

 5) The scratch, gouge or corrosion must be more than 0.25 inches from a primary
 fusion welded joint.
 6) If the damage to the ducts do not have these conditions, replace the ducts.

 (b) Procedure 4 is for heavily blocked drain lines.
 (2) A blockage in the lavatory or the galley drain is possible if unwanted materials get in the
 system. If you permit only the waste water in the drains, this type of blockage will not occur.
 (a) In Rumbold or YRC lavatories, the vent holes are just above the toilet paper roll holder.

 cabinet.

 disassembling the drain line sections if applicable.

titulo: Standard Practices for the Proper Handling of Toilet Waste.
procedimento:
(1) You must obey local regulatory procedures and company policies when working with toilet
 waste and toilet waste equipment.
SUBTASK 38-32-00-912-061

 (1) When servicing or maintaining the toilet system and its components, make sure you wear the
 applicable personal protection equipment such as the following:
 (a) Elbow length gloves
 (b) Face Mask
 (c) Safety Glasses
 (d) Disposable gowns or other protective clothing considered appropriate for the handling of
 toilet waste.
 SUBTASK 38-32-00-912-062

 (2) You must thoroughly disinfect anything you come in contact with when working with toilet
 waste.

 38-32-00

 THOROUGHLY WITH SOAP AND WATER AFTER COMPLETION OF WASTE
 SYSTEM PROCEDURES. DO NOT SERVICE POTABLE WATER SYSTEMS, OR
 CONDUCT MAINTENANCE ON ANY POTABLE WATER SYSTEM COMPONENTS
 CONCURRENTLY AFTER CONDUCTING SUCH OPERATIONS WITHOUT WASHING
 HANDS. FAILURE TO DO SO CAN CAUSE ILLNESS TO OTHERS OR SELF.
 (3) You must thoroughly disinfect yourself and your clothing before working on other aircraft
 components.

 components after servicing or maintaining the toilet waste system and its components

 (4) Thoroughly clean and disinfect any toilet waste system components removed from the airplane
 prior to normal handling and shipping operations.

 (f) Precautions - Air Separation Module
 (2) The NGS is an inert gas system that decreases the flammability of the center tank. Fresh air
 has approximately 78% nitrogen and 21% oxygen. The NGS separates the fresh air into two
 components: Nitrogen-Enriched Air (NEA) and Oxygen-Enriched Air (OEA). NEA is the
 increase of nitrogen gas and decrease of the oxygen in the air. If you breathe air that does not
 have sufficient oxygen, health problems can occur. Obey the precautions in this procedure if
 you do maintenance in an area where you could breathe air that does not have sufficient
 oxygen.
 (3) The NGS components are found in the air conditioning compartment on the left side of the
 airplane. Access to the Thermal Control Unit (TCU) and Air Separation Module (ASM) is
 through access door 3302L. The Nitrogen-Enriched Air Distribution System (NEADS) line is
 attached to the ASM and is routed to the center tank through approximately the center of the
 main wheel well. The NEADS line has 0.5 in. (1.3 cm) aluminum tubing, a dielectric isolator
 hose, a flame arrestor, check valves, and a float valve.
 (4) Operation of the NGS causes air in the fuel tank to decrease the oxygen contents. Do not
 breathe the air in the fuel tank unless that tank is fully ventilated. Procedures for fuel tank
 purging and entry on airplanes equipped with a NGS are given in CHAPTER 28. Danger
 stencils and placards are installed adjacent to the access doors on the fuel tank. This is to
 warn personnel of the hazards if they breathe air with low oxygen content.
 (5) NEA that is generated by the ASM is routed safely to the center tank. The usual operation of
 the NGS outside of the fuel tanks is free from concentrations of NEA. However, a duct leak, or
 component failure can cause NEA to go into areas outside of the fuel tanks. An NEA leak can
 cause a condition where the oxygen content of the air is decreased. Caution stencils and
 placards are installed on access doors adjacent to areas where potential NEA leakage can
 occur.

 menu item, ACTIVE: YES/NO, is provided.
 (3) Existing faults are listed in reverse chronological order (the most recent fault listed first).

(1) This task gives the instructions to operate the BDU control panel for the Fault History Menu.
 (2) To help navigate through the NGS BDU fault history structure, refer to Figure 207.
 (3) The fault history menu allows you to look at NGS faults and correlated flight deck effects that
 occurred during the last 99 flight legs. The flight leg is updated during the ground to air (WOW)
 transition.
 (4) Fault history can store up to 256 messages. No more than 25% of the fault history can be
 allocated to a single flight leg. If a single flight leg fault allocation is full, no additional fault
 records can be recorded for that flight leg. When the total allocation of faults is full, new faults
 will replace the oldest fault.

(1) This task gives the instructions to operate the BDU control panel for the BDU Ground Test
 Menu.
 (2) To help you scroll through the BDU ground test structure, refer to Figure 208.
 (3) The BDU ground test menu supplies the controls to do three types of BDU manually Initiated
 Built-In-Tests (IBIT). The IBIT tests include these ground tests:
 (a) System IBIT
 (b) Electrical IBIT
 (c) NGS performance IBIT
 (4) BDU System IBIT (System Test?)
 (a) The BDU system test is manually initiated test done by the NGS controller when the NGS
 system is pressurized. To do the system test, it is necessary to pressurize the NGS with
 bleed air pressure and operate the left air conditioning pack. The system test is a timed
 sequence test that does a check of the open and closed position of all of the electrically
 controlled valves. This includes the NGS shutoff valve, ram air valve, overtemperature
 shutoff valve and the ASM high-flow valve. The system test also does a test of the filter
 pressure switch and a test for sensor drift for the NGS bleed pressure sensor.
 (b) The NGS controller will not start the test (test inhibited) or once started, stop the test (test
 aborted), if the airplane configuration is incorrect. This includes: NGS inlet pressure less
 than 15 psig (103 kPa), the airplane in air mode, the packs are off, the center tank refuel
 valves open, or an invalid aircraft ID.
 (c) The NGS controller will also not start the test if an NGS sensor that is used to control the
 open/closed position of a valve is out of limits. The test will not start if there are existing
 fault messages. The NGS controller will also inhibit the test if a controller valve driver, or
 valve solenoid/torque motor is inoperative.
 (d) When the system test is started, the NGS controller monitors the NGS system
 performance. The NGS controller will stop the test if there is a change in the airplane
 configuration as noted in the previous step. Other events that will cause the test to stop
 include an overtemperature condition or an NGS fault is detected by the controller. The
 test can also be stopped manually if the MENU or ON/OFF push button controls are
 pushed during the test. If the system test is stopped before the test is fully done, all
 latched system faults that were present prior to the start of the system test will continue to
 be recorded as latched faults.

(1) Corrosion evaluation will be required after initial inspection and cleaning to determine the
 nature and extent of the repair or rework.
 It is difficult to establish a distinct and specific dividing line between various conditions.
 Consequently, the first requirement for evaluation is a good, and sound, maintenance
 judgment.
 B. Evaluate any corrosion as follows:
 SUBTASK 51-00-53-212-017

 (1) LIGHT CORROSION - Characterized by a discoloration or pitting of the surface to a depth of
 approximately 0.001 inch (0.025 mm) maximum.
 This type of damage will normally be removed by a light hand sanding or a minimal chemical
 treatment.
 SUBTASK 51-00-53-212-018

 (2) MODERATE CORROSION - This corrosion appears similar to LIGHT CORROSION except
 that there may be some blistering, or evidence of scaling and flaking. Pitting depths may be as
 deep as 0.010 inch (0.254 mm). This type of corrosion damage will normally be removed by
 extensive hand or mechanical sanding.
 SUBTASK 51-00-53-212-019

 (3) HEAVY (SEVERE) CORROSION - The general appearance may be similar to MODERATE
 CORROSION with severe blistering, exfoliation and scaling or flaking. Pitting depths will be
 deeper than 0.010 inch (0.254 mm). This type of corrosion damage will normally be removed
 by extensive mechanical sanding or grinding, or replacement.

(1) Corrosion can be removed by mechanical or chemical procedures. Examples of mechanical
 removal are:
 (a) Hand sanding with an abrasive paper or metal-wool.
 (b) Power sanding or buffing with abrasive pads.
 (c) Grinding wheels and abrasive blasting with compressed air, which includes abrasive

 therefore, necessary that any corrosion removal is done completely.

(1) Bare surfaces of carbon (alloy) steels are highly reactive when exposed to the environment.
 Carbon steel is either cadmium or cadmiumtitanium plated after machining and heat treated.
 (2) Steel parts absorb hydrogen during processing operations and in service when hydrogen may
 be produced and diffused into the metal.
 Hydrogen absorption, can cause crack initiation and propagation, resulting in delayed brittle
 fracturing when the part is under sustained tensile strength.
 (3) The susceptibility of carbon steel parts to hydrogen embrittlement increases as hardness and
 strength increases.
 (4) Steel parts heat-treated to 180 ksi, and below, are not considered susceptible to hydrogen
 embrittlement, while steel parts heat- treated to 220 ksi, and above, are highly susceptible to
 hydrogen embrittlement and must be plated by low embrittlement processes.

titulo: Top Guide Plate Latch Pin Hole Repair
procedimento:
(1) This task is a repair of the hole for the latch pin in the top guide plate. The repair installs a
 stainless steel bushing to make the hole the correct dimension.
SUBTASK 52-11-00-018-002

 (1) Get access to the latch pin hole in the top guide plate.
 (a) Remove the bolts that hold the top guide plate.
 (b) Move the top guide plate sufficiently to get to the hole for the latch pin.
 (c) You can remove the top guide plate as an alternative.
 SUBTASK 52-11-00-228-003

 (2) Measure the latch pin hole.

 52-11-00

 D6-37569 Sep 25/2015

 (a) The latch pin hole is satisfactory if the diameter is less than 0.4078 inch.
 NOTE: If the latch pin hole is satisfactory, do not do the remaining steps in this task.
 (b) Repair the latch pin hole if the diameter is more than 0.4078 inch.
 SUBTASK 52-11-00-328-004

 (3) Make a spotface at the latch pin hole.
 (a) Make the depth of the spotface 0.080 inch.
 (b) Make the diameter of the spotface 0.593 inch.
 SUBTASK 52-11-00-358-005

 (4) Make a bushing.
 (a) Use the piece of 17-4PH stainless steel to make the bushing.
 (b) Make the thickness of the bushing the same as the depth of the spotface.
 (c) Make the inner diameter of the bushing 0.3438 to 0.3478 inch.
 (d) Make the outer diameter of the bushing larger than the outer diameter of the spotface by
 0.0015 to 0.0020 inch.
 (e) Heat-treat the bushing.
 1) Increase the temperature of the bushing to 900 degrees F for one hour.
 2) Let the temperature of the bushing decrease in the air.
 SUBTASK 52-11-00-428-006

 (5) Install the bushing in the top guide plate.
 (a) Put the bushing in the spotface.
 (b) Put coating, C00064 on the area of the repair (PAGEBLOCK 51-21-41/701).
 (c) Put the primer, C00259 on the area of the repair (PAGEBLOCK 51-21-99/701).
 SUBTASK 52-11-00-418-007

 (6) Install the top guide plate.
 (a) Move the top guide plate to align the holes for the bolts.
 (b) Install the bolts in the top guide plate.

(1) You can repair cracks that are less than 45 degrees away from the centerline of the door stop
 fitting. If the crack is not in this area, you must replace the stop fitting.
SUBTASK 52-13-00-028-013

 (1) Remove the bearing plate.
 SUBTASK 52-13-00-218-014

 (b) Make a spotface in the stop fitting to give a 0.002 to 0.012 inch clearance with the
 bearing plate.
 (c) Prepare the surfaces (Method III) and apply Alodine (PAGEBLOCK 51-21-41/701 and
 PAGEBLOCK 51-21-21/701).

 (a) Turn the instrument on with the toggle switch or the button in the handle.
 (b) Hold the sensor head at least 12 inches (305mm) away from any object and push the null
 button to zero the instrument.
 NOTE: If you release the handle button or turn the instrument off, you must zero the

 adjusted.

 SUBTASK 53-52-00-286-018

 (6) Moisture Meter Inspection Method
 (a) Put the sensor head on the inner surface of the radome.
 1) Make sure that all the electrodes contact the radome surface.
 2) If necessary, apply light force to make sure the sensor head contacts the radome
 surface.
 (b) Move the sensor head over all of the inner surface of the radome. The sensor head must
 touch the full inner surface of the radome. To perform an adequate inspection, the sensor
 must be indexed at an interval of 1 inch (25.4mm) or less.
 (c) In areas that cause a meter reading of 20 or greater, put the sensor head away from the
 center of the indication (in an adjacent area with a reading of less than 20). Monitor the
 meter reading as you move the sensor head toward the center of the area.
 (d) To identify the area of entrapped water, make marks on the radome at the position of the
 electrodes closest to the entrapped water when the meter reading increases to 20.
 1) Do these steps until the boundary of the entrapped water is marked.
 (e) If the area that you marked is greater than the allowable area shown in Table 601,
 remove the moisture in the marked area and seal it (SRM 53-10-72).

procedimento:
(1) Rub with abrasive paper, polish, or buff the No. 2 or No. 3 (acrylic) windows to remove

 (3) Put a Spraylat SC-1071 coating, C50135 protective coating or Protex 20V tape, G00139 on the
 areas of the window that do not have scratches.

SUBTASK 56-11-21-228-004

 (1) Use an micrometer, COM-2039 to measure the depth of scratches or crazing.

 window.

 silicon carbide sandpaper, G50221 or cloth. Use a coarse abrasive paper for gauges, deep
 scratches, and bad crazing (usually not more than 100 grit).
 NOTE: If a small repair is necessary, use a fine abrasive paper to reduce the time to polish the
 window. Do not try to repair only a local part of the surface area. This will cause visual
 distortion.
 SUBTASK 56-11-21-178-008

 (5) Flush away the grit and acrylic material with water.
 NOTE: Use sufficient water to keep the window surface cool.

 approximately 800 cycles per minute.

(1) General No. 2 Window Vocabulary
 (a) Window Components
 1) Acrylic Wafers: Acrylic Wafers are used to hold the temperature sensor wires in its
 position. The sensor pack consists of acrylic wafers that attach the filament wires
 that stabilizes the wire grid and lets the part to be moved while being made.
 2) Fail-Safe Interlayer: Interlayer that will hold the pressure loads if there is a failure of
 a structural pane.
 3) Interlayer: A flexible transparent layer that bonds glass panes together. It can be a
 structural component for pressure fail-safety and bird impact resistance.
 4) Laminate: Assembly of interlayer materials and glass panes bonded together by
 application of heat and pressure.
 5) Metal Insert: A thin piece of metal around the periphery of the window used to
 transfer failsafe pressure or bird impact loads from the interlayer to the window
 installation fasteners.
 6) Pane: One layer of glass or acrylic in a window.
 7) Pressure Seal: A rubber gasket that makes a pressure seal between the window
 and the fuselage.
 8) Slip planes or Release Tape: Transparent material embedded in the interlayer
 around the periphery of some Triplex ( XXX,) or Sierracin made windows. The
 internal tape is almost transparent, but can include visible wrinkles, usually in the
 corners of the windows. The internal tape does not in the PPG made windows.
 9) Structural Pane: A glass pane that holds the pressure loads of the window.
 10) Urethane: A type of interlayer material.
 11) Vinyl (Polyvinyl Butyral or PVB): A type of interlayer material.
 12) Z Seal: A Z-shaped piece of metal that is bonded to the window edge. The seal is a
 barrier used to prevent external moisture penetration into the window laminate.
 (b) Window Vision Terms
 1) Clear View Area (Daylight Opening or DLO): The transparent area of the window for
 external vision.
 2) Critical Vision Area: The area of primary vision through the window that does not
 include the Non-Critical Vision Area.

(1) If the window is damaged as specified in this procedure, remove the window and replace or
 repair the damaged components (PAGEBLOCK 56-21-00/401).
 (2) Do the passenger cabin window inspection.
 (a) Crack:
 A crack is not a complete break but it has width when you look parallel to the face of the
 crack. A crack can occur at any angle to the surface of the prismatic pane. The direction
 of the crack depends on the direction of the applied force. The stress from a scratch or a
 craze can cause a crack to occur.
 (b) Crazing:
 A crazed prismatic pane has a number of very thin cracks which are 90 degrees to the
 surface of the prismatic pane. Because the cracks are very thin, it is not easy to see the
 crazing.
 When you look at the prismatic pane at different angles, you can see the crazing by its
 reflection on the smooth surface of the prismatic pane.
 (c) In-plane Cracking (delamination)
 In-plane cracking can be a smooth fissure, or group of fissures that can occur along the
 surface of the pane. In-plane cracks can occur in acrylic. The cracks start at the edges of
 the pane or in the center of the pane. You can best find the cracks with a reflection of light
 from the smooth surfaces of the fissure.
 (d) Scratch:
 A scratch occurs when there is removal of material from the surface of the prismatic pane
 along a line. Scratches are divided into tree types: superficial, minor, and major.
 Superficial scratches are less than 0.001 inch in depth. This type of scratch is caused
 when the window is not cleaned carefully. Minor scratches are from 0.001 to 0.003 inch in
 depth. Major scratches are greater than 0.004 inch in depth.
 (e) Chips:
 A chip occurs when there is removal of material from the surface of the prismatic pane
 not along a line. The chip in the prismatic pane can have a circular shape or a "V" shape.
